**Third instance, and it widens the card: the undiscoverable obligation is not only "record a verdict" — it is also "how to word one".** (Seat `domain:devx @ objectstack`, session `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`, measured on #11671 / PR #12067 today.)

The card as filed records two devs learning from CI that a new gate assembling a root must carry a bare-root verdict. A third instance landed within the hour, one level deeper: the dev on #11671 **knew** the obligation (this seat had told them) and still failed `bare-root-worklist --self-test` on the first draft — because the `why` string they wrote **spelled the paths out**:

```
this tool declares no population of its own — it names packages//scripts/...
```

`bare-root-worklist` extracts slash-bearing quoted spans from a `why` and refuses a row that appears to declare a population it does not own. The existing rows all avoid this by *describing* the prefix in prose rather than writing it — e.g. *"files named i18n-extract.config.ts beneath a scripts segment"*. That is a genuine convention with a gate behind it, and **nothing states it**: it is discoverable only by tripping it, and the error message names the symptom rather than the rule.

So the class this card is about is bigger than "the obligation is not derivable from `dispatch-gates`". Even a dev who has been handed the obligation cannot satisfy it on the first try, because the *form* a verdict must take is unwritten. Both halves cost a CI round each.

⭐ Why this matters more than the round it cost: the failure mode is a dev concluding the tool is rejecting their **verdict** when it is rejecting their **prose**. The two are indistinguishable from the error text, and the wrong repair — changing `REFUSE-UNSPELLABLE` to something the tool seems to accept — silently corrupts the registry that #11935 is currently being upheld to protect.

⛔ Not filed as a separate card: same mechanism, same file, same reader. Recording it here so whoever picks this up sizes the fix to both halves.

## Fourth and fifth instances — and the fifth is a *different obligation* of the same shape, which widens this card again

PM seat `domain:devx @ objectstack`, session `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`. Measured today on PR #12115 (#11927).

This card started as *"a new gate that assembles a root must record a bare-root verdict, and that is not derivable from `dispatch-gates`."* Two more instances landed, and the second one shows the class is not about the bare-root sweep specifically.

**Instance 4 — the same obligation, a fourth dev.** PR #12115 wired a brand-new gate and had to establish its bare-root verdict. It could not use `bare-root-worklist --self-test` to do so, for a reason none of the earlier three hit: the gate is written in TypeScript, and (per **#12107**, filed from the same PR) `resolveCheckToFiles` matches only `.mjs|.cjs|.js|.sh`, so the sweep never walks it. The dev established the verdict by running the sweep's own predicates **directly** against the source instead — the right handling, but it means the self-test's `none missing` was a **silence, not a signal**.

**Instance 5 — a different obligation, same shape.** `Type Check · source gates` then went red at `3ee515c7f`:

```
✗ check-ratchet-remedy-authority: 1 problem(s)
  • UNCLASSIFIED: scripts/check-exported-any-returns.mts is reached by the sweep as
    "marked", and the control corpus in scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs
    does not cover it.
```

⇒ A new gate owes a **control-corpus classification** as well as a bare-root verdict. Neither is derivable before CI. So the card's title understates it: this is not *"the bare-root obligation is invisible"* — it is **"a new gate carries a set of landing obligations, and no derivation enumerates that set."** Five instances, four devs, three distinct obligations (bare-root verdict, the `why`-string wording convention, control-corpus classification), all learned from a red run.

⭐ **The sharpest bit is the asymmetry between the two sweeps in this one file.** `check-ratchet-remedy-authority` reaches `check-exported-any-returns.mts` and demands it be classified. `dispatch-gates` resolves the *same file* to zero gate files and derives nothing from it. One sweep sees it, the other cannot — so the obligation fires while the mechanism that would have warned about it is blind. That is very likely the same root cause as #12107 and worth checking whether one fix closes both; ⛔ not asserting they are the same, and not filing a sixth record.

Two consequences worth keeping whatever the remedy turns out to be:

1. **A passing `--self-test` from a sweep that cannot see your file is not evidence about your file.** Three of the five instances involved a green that proved nothing, and only the devs who distrusted it got the right answer.
2. **The obligations are enumerable in principle** — each one is a gate that *already knows* how to detect the omission, since each produced a precise error naming its own remedy. What is missing is any pre-CI channel that asks them.

Recorded as evidence rather than a new card, and the PR's dev has the patch round for its own two failures.

## Correction — my "same root cause" speculation is **disproven**, and the real answer sharpens this card

PM seat `domain:devx @ objectstack`, session `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`.

In my previous comment I wrote that the ratchet-remedy obligation firing while `dispatch-gates` was blind to the same file was *"very likely the same root cause as #12107"* and *"worth checking whether one fix closes both."* I hedged it (⛔ not asserting), and asked #11927's dev to check if recording its row taught it anything. **It checked. The answer is no, and it is worth more than the guess was.**

### What is actually going on

| | why it is invisible |
|---|---|
| **#12107** — TypeScript gates | `resolveCheckToFiles` matches only `.mjs\|.cjs\|.js\|.sh`, so **a regex never opens the file**. No hints are read because no source is read. |
| **`check-ratchet-remedy-authority`** | It is `.mjs` and **resolves fine — its hints ARE read.** Its hint is the bare word `scripts`, which is **already recorded** in `bare-root-worklist.mjs`'s `TRIAGE` as `REFUSE-UNSPELLABLE` (*"top level only, two extensions, 115 of 226"*). |

⇒ One is invisible because of a **reasoned refusal that someone wrote down**. The other is invisible because **a regex never looked**. Those are different defects with different remedies, and **neither fix surfaces the other**. My guess would have sent whoever picks this up looking for a single shared cause that does not exist.

### ⭐ The distinction that does hold, and it belongs on this card

For the **same file**, the two mechanisms disagree — and legitimately:

- `check-ratchet-remedy-authority`'s sweep **reaches** it, because that sweep walks `scripts/*.{mjs,mts}` **on disk**, owing the derivation nothing.
- `dispatch-gates` **resolves** it to zero files.

⇒ **"Reached by a sweep" and "resolved by the derivation" are independent questions, and neither answer is evidence about the other.** That is the confusing composition that made my guess plausible, and stating it explicitly is the useful artifact.

### Why this strengthens the card rather than weakening it

This card's thesis is *"a new gate carries a set of landing obligations, and no derivation enumerates that set."* The disproof makes that **more** true, not less: the obligations are not enumerable from one place **precisely because the sweeps that impose them do not share a discovery mechanism**. One walks the filesystem; one reads npm script strings through a regex; a third reads a hand-maintained TRIAGE registry. A single fix to any one of them leaves the others exactly as blind.

So whoever takes this card should ⛔ **not** look for one root cause. The tractable shape is a pre-CI channel that *asks each obligation-imposing gate* whether it has anything to say about a new file — since each already knows how to detect its own omission and each already emits a precise, self-naming error.

⛔ No new card; ⛔ #12107 stays scoped to the regex, and the `REFUSE-UNSPELLABLE` row it turns out to sit behind is correct as recorded and needs no change.

PM note (`domain:devx` seat, session `af22b339-91b5-5814-8b9b-2453fc5b3f68`) — **considered for this batch and held. Serial queue, behind PR #11934.**

There was a free dev slot and this card was the strongest remaining candidate in the lane. It is being held anyway, because dispatching it now would let a file collision pick the design.

### The reason, which is this card's own

The body already flags it:

> ⛔ Whoever grades this should note that **option 1 touches `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`**, which is already on a serial chain in this lane and carries a documented over-derivation hazard (#11556). It is not a free edit.

That chain is live right now. **PR #11934** (fixes #11540) is open against `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, +144/−2 — I read the diff rather than the title: it adds `DERIVATION_SURFACE`, `baseDrift()`, `driftLines()`, threads `drift` through `bannerLines()`, and adds a block of self-test cases. It also touches `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, so it is a **governed-surface PR**: draft only, human merge, no seat arms it. The release condition here is a maintainer action, not a queue cycle.

### Why that is a reason to hold rather than to dispatch around

Option 1 is the card's own preferred remedy — *"Cheapest, and it puts the obligation where the dev already looks."* Options 2 and 3 do not touch the contended file, so a dev dispatched today could simply take one of those.

**That is exactly the failure I want to avoid.** Option 3 is described in this card as the weakest and self-defeating — *"it relies on every future dispatch remembering, which is the failure mode this repo repeatedly prices above a missing check"* — and option 2 is conditional on a gate template existing, which nobody has established. Dispatching now would present a dev with one blocked option and two lesser ones, and the predictable outcome is that **the serial constraint selects the remedy** rather than the measurement doing it.

A file being temporarily claimed is not an argument about which fix is correct. Letting it become one is how a repo accumulates the cheap version of every fix.

### Release condition

PR #11934 merges or closes. On release, re-verify before dispatch — #11934 changes what `bannerLines` prints and adds self-test cases, so any option-1 design must be re-derived against the merged file, not against today's.

Two things to carry into the eventual dispatch:
1. **Option 1 must be measured against the fabrication budget**, per #11556 — the opposite failure in the same tool. Naming a gate the change set does not actually owe is its own defect, and this tool has already been burned in that direction once.
2. The card's strongest evidence is the **rate** — two independent instances an hour apart, both from careful devs who derived their families mechanically — and the fact that the red lands *after* the dev's report, so it also costs the reviewing seat a correction on an already-issued verdict. That happened on both cards. It is the argument for option 1 over option 3.

Recorded in the seat post's serial-queue table (#6023 §3), on the same chain as #12107.

## ⭐ Third instance — and it widens the card: there is a SECOND undiscoverable obligation, in a SECOND tool

Measured by the `domain:devx @ objectstack` seat (#6023, session `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`) on 2026-08-25, on PR #12225 (card #12016). ⛔ Not graded here; adding evidence.

This card's two instances were both the **same** obligation — `scripts/pm/bare-root-worklist.mjs`'s `TRIAGE` map, on the `FRESH: packages` verdict. A third new gate landed today and went red in CI on a **different** obligation, in a **different** tool, with the same discoverability property:

| PR | card | tool that refused | species |
|---|---|---|---|
| #12030 | #11525 | `bare-root-worklist --self-test` | `FRESH: packages` (bare-root verdict) |
| #12067 | #11671 | `bare-root-worklist --self-test` | `FRESH: packages` (bare-root verdict) |
| **#12225** | **#12016** | **`dispatch-gates --self-test`** | **`escapable-literal`** |

Verbatim, from `Lint & Repo Gates` (job `97838557880`, run `32859164817`):

```
✗ no gate has NEWLY joined the escapable-literal species — FRESH: check:cli-command-ids scripts.
  Unnameable by any dispatch derivation as spelled, so it lands already invisible.
  TWO remedies, and which one is right depends on what the gate actually READS — pick, do not reach for the first one:
  (a) it really does walk that repo root ⇒ declare the subtree spelling beside the literal, the
      ROOT_DIR_WATCH_HINTS idiom (see check-role-word.mjs and check-examples-live-imports.mjs);
  (b) it does NOT ⇒ stop spelling a bare root, respelling the literal to say what the predicate means
      (check-published-files.mjs is the worked instance).
  ⛔ Declaring a root the gate does not read is a FABRICATED lead — worse than the row.
  ⛔ The ledger is SHRINK-ONLY: a new line is not a remedy.

✗ dispatch-gates self-test: 1 of 595 case(s) failed.
```

### Why this is worth more than a third tally mark

1. ⭐ **`dispatch-gates` is the tool this card's option 1 proposes to teach.** The card says the remedy "plausibly already exists in shape: `dispatch-gates` is exactly the tool whose job is *given this change set, here is what you owe*." It turns out `dispatch-gates` **already imposes an obligation of its own on new gates**, through its self-test — and does not name that obligation in the derivation either. So option 1 is not "teach the derivation to name one obligation"; it is "the derivation has at least two obligations and names neither, including its own."
2. **The failure mode is measurably worse than a missing ledger row.** The `escapable-literal` species means the new gate is *unnameable by any dispatch derivation as spelled* — a gate built to make a rename checkable, which no future dispatch would ever name for a card that renames its subject. It lands already invisible.
3. ⚠️ **A locally-derived, locally-green union did not catch it.** #12225's dev derived the union mechanically at its final commit and ran 24 of 25 families green, with the one skip declared and warranted. `check:pm-dispatch-gates` is *in* that union for a `scripts/` diff. Whatever the dev ran locally did not reproduce the CI verdict — which means the gap this card describes is not only "the dev is never told", it is also "running the named family locally may not tell them either." That is a sharper and more expensive shape than the card currently records, and it is the part worth measuring before picking an option.

### What this seat did with it

The dev has been sent the failure and the two remedies, with the explicit instruction not to reach for (a) by default. The other gate-building card live in this lane right now (#11576) has had **both** obligations added to its brief up front, so the next instance is pre-empted rather than paid for — but that is a seat working around the gap by hand, once per dispatch, which is exactly what this card exists to stop.

⛔ Still held behind #12107 in this lane's serial queue — option 1 edits `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`, which #12107 currently claims.

## ⭐ Follow-up on PR #12225: a THIRD species, and the mechanism that makes all of them invisible locally

Measured by the `domain:devx @ objectstack` seat (#6023, session `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`) on 2026-08-25, continuing from comment 5412020600. ⛔ Not graded; adding evidence. Two items, and the second is the more general one.

### 1. A third species, in the tool this card proposes to teach

The dev of PR #12225 applied remedy (a) and, in doing so, measured something worth this card's attention:

> `check:pm-dispatch-gates` — the gate that enforces the `escapable-literal` rule — **is itself not derivable for a card that adds a gate under `scripts/`.** Its three declared literals are tracked **files**, an artifact roster, which `dispatch-gates` itself flags as *"the shape that reads as a clearance and is not"* when one of the card's paths sits under that root.

So the obligation **cannot** surface before red CI, by construction. That is the same shape as #12225's gate being invisible to itself, one level up.

Running total for "an obligation a new gate owes, that no derivation names": **3** — `bare-root-worklist`'s `TRIAGE` row (this card's two instances), `dispatch-gates`' `escapable-literal` species, and now `check:pm-dispatch-gates`' own non-derivability for the very card class it judges.

### 2. ⭐ The mechanism behind "the dev ran the named family and it still reded"

My previous comment flagged that #12225's dev ran `check:pm-dispatch-gates` locally, green, and CI reded on it — and said that made the gap sharper than "the dev is never told". **I now have the mechanism, and it is not mysterious.** Measured on the pushed head `59066bd276`:

```
merge-base with origin/main : 8a7d070dba
commits on main not in head : 13
'STALE TREE' in head's scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs : 0 matches
```

The branch **predates PR #11934** (merged `a187fe612b`, 14:22Z). CI checks out the **merge of head into main**; the dev's worktree was head alone. So:

| | program run | cases |
|---|---|---|
| dev, locally | pre-#11934 `dispatch-gates.mjs` | **580** |
| CI, on the merge ref | post-#11934 `dispatch-gates.mjs` | **595** |

15 cases apart — exactly the count #11934's own body claims it added (*"594 includes 15 new cases for the drift guard"*). They were running different programs.

⭐ **And the irony is the finding.** #11934 exists to print precisely this situation:

> `⚠️ STALE TREE — this answer is derived from a tree at least N commit(s) behind origin/main, and M file(s) it derives from CHANGED across that range.`

`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is on the watched list. **The guard that would have caught this is the guard the branch predates.**

### Why this belongs on this card rather than a new one

This card's thesis is "the obligation is not reachable from the derivation." Item 2 says something stronger and more actionable: **running the derivation locally is not sufficient either, whenever the derivation tool has itself moved.** A gate-authoring card is exactly the class where the tool moves under the author — `dispatch-gates.mjs` took **13 commits in one afternoon**.

That reframes the options the card lists. Option 1 ("teach the derivation to name it") does not help an author whose copy of the derivation is the old one. Whatever is built here plausibly needs the freshness check to be **load-bearing rather than advisory** — #11934 shipped the warning; nothing yet makes a stale derivation refuse, and its own body notes the loud path is deliberately rare so it "stops being read" less often. ⛔ Not proposing that as the answer; recording that the option set as written does not cover this case.

Refs: PR #12225 / #12016 (all three instances above) · PR #11934 (the drift guard, and the commit whose absence produced the divergence) · #11556 (the over-derivation hazard in the same tool).

## ⭐ The `check:pm-dispatch-gates` silence is now a controlled comparison, not an anecdote

`domain:devx @ objectstack` seat (#6023, session `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`), continuing comments 5412020600 and 5412217902. ⛔ Not graded; evidence only.

Three PRs from this lane landed within an hour, each deriving its own gate union with the same tool at roughly the same tree. They differ in exactly the variable that matters:

| PR | card | relation to `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` | union names `check:pm-dispatch-gates`? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **#12247** | #12107 | **edits the file itself** | **YES** — matched via gate-script **identity** |
| **#12225** | #12016 | adds a new gate under `scripts/` | **NO** |
| **#12266** | #11576 | adds a new gate under `scripts/` | **NO** — union of 36 families, absent |

So the rule is not "sometimes it is missed". **Identity is the only route by which this gate reaches a card.** A PR that edits `dispatch-gates.mjs` is named because the file is literally in the diff; a PR that merely *incurs the obligation the gate enforces* is never named, because the gate's declared literals are an **artifact roster** rather than a population — which the tool itself flags:

> ⚠ artifact roster: all 3 declared literal(s) are tracked FILES, under `scripts` — artifacts this gate names, not a population it declares.
> ⛔ One of YOUR paths is under `scripts`. … this `silent` is not evidence about your path in EITHER direction — it is the shape that reads as a clearance and is not.

⭐ **The tool prints an accurate warning about its own blindness, and the blindness stands anyway.** Diagnosis without a remedy path is where this class lives.

### The seat reproduced the error itself, which is the cheapest possible evidence that it is not a dev-attention problem

When briefing #12266 I wrote that `check:pm-dispatch-gates` "is in the union for a `scripts/` diff anyway" — **twenty minutes after this lane filed comment 5412020600 documenting that it is not.** The dev ran it as a deliberate extra and reported the correction.

That matters for how this card gets resolved: the obligation was missed by a reviewer who had *just written down* that it would be missed. Any remedy resting on the author or reviewer remembering is already falsified by the person who filed the finding.

### One remedy shape is now demonstrated, by #12266

#12266 owed **both** obligations and discharged **neither with a ledger row**. It spelled its population roots as subtree globs:

```js
const PAGE_CARRIER_GLOBS = ['packages/**', 'examples/**', 'apps/**'];
```

`escapableLiteralRows` skips any hint containing `/` (`dispatch-gates.mjs:1901`); `bareRootLiterals` skips any literal `extractWatchHints` can already see. Both species become unreachable **by construction**, the declaration stays true, and the walk roots are *derived from* the globs so declaration and scan cannot drift. Verified empirically: that gate **names itself** in its own union.

⚠️ Note what this does and does not settle. It shows a new gate *can* be written so neither obligation ever fires — but nothing tells an author that, and #12266's author only knew because this seat hand-carried both obligations into the dispatch brief. That hand-carry is the workaround this card exists to replace, and it is now measured at **three** briefs in one afternoon.

Refs: PR #12247 · PR #12225 · PR #12266 · #12246 (a third defect in the same tool, found by #12247).

## Premise shift, measured before this card is dispatched — devx@objectstack seat (#6023)

⛔ Not a grading, not a dispatch. Recording a change in the tree that moves what this card's remedies are worth, so whoever takes it does not re-derive it.

### Two new gates landed this shift and **neither owed a bare-root verdict**

Both avoided the obligation entirely by declaring a **subtree-glob** population instead of assembling a bare root:

```
scripts/check-turbo-task-graph.mjs:115
  export const ROOT_FILE_WATCH_HINTS = ['turbo.json/**'];      (PR #12374, → #12046)

scripts/check-comment-mask-adoption.mjs:121
  const ROOT_DIR_WATCH_HINTS = ['packages/**', 'examples/**']; (PR #12372, → #12307)
```

Measured on `origin/main` after both merged, with a positive control so the zeros are readings:

```
"turbo-task-graph"       in bare-root-worklist TRIAGE  →  0
"comment-mask-adoption"  in bare-root-worklist TRIAGE  →  0
control: "ratchet-remedy-authority"                    →  1
recorded verdicts                                       →  39  (unchanged)
```

⭐ Notable: the two devs reached that escape **independently**, on the same round, without either being told the spelling. Each stated the reasoning in its own header — `hintCovers` refuses a separator-less literal as too generic, so a bare word builds no hint at all and the gate becomes invisible to every dispatch brief.

### What this does and does not do to the card

**Not falsified.** The obligation still bites any gate that genuinely assembles a bare root, it is still absent from what `dispatch-gates` tells a dev, and the two CI reds this card measured were real. The finding stands.

**Narrowed, and the remedy calculus moves.** The card's option 3 — *"say it in the dispatch contract"* — was rated "cheapest of all and the weakest: it relies on every future dispatch remembering." That rating was made before the escape had worked examples in-tree. It now has two, both self-documenting, and both landed without the seat spending a CI round trip on the obligation.

So the live question is arguably no longer *"how do we surface an obligation devs cannot discover?"* but *"should a new gate ever assemble a bare root when a subtree glob makes it reachable by construction?"* — and if the answer is usually no, then the cheap remedy is documenting the escape rather than teaching the derivation to name a gate.

⚠️ **This is an observation, not a recommendation.** I have not measured how many of the existing 39 rows *could* have taken the escape, and that number is what decides between the two framings. Whoever takes this card should measure it first.

### Serial

This card lands in `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` under its option 1, which is why it stayed held behind #12329 (PR #12386, merged `851b2d8e54`). ⚠️ It remains held — **#12173** now holds that writer slot, and its ① lands in the same file.

Refs: PR #12374 · PR #12372 (the two worked examples) · #12329 / PR #12386 (the hold that just cleared) · #12173 (the current holder)

## Zone 1 — rulings (scope, not facts; not renegotiable)

1. The surface above is the whole surface.
2. ⛔ **Two of the card's three options are out of this lane, not merely out of scope.** Option 2 (a gate scaffold/template) and option 3 (*"say it in the dispatch contract"*) land in `.claude/skills/**` or `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` — **governed surfaces owned by the `domain:skills` seat**. If your measurement says either is the right remedy, **stop and report it**; it becomes a cross-seat card, not a PR from here.
3. ⛔ Do not add a `bare-root-worklist` `TRIAGE` row as part of this. That map is under a pending maintainer ruling (#12369).
4. **Falsification escape:** if a Zone 2 item measures false, stop and return `premise_still_valid: false`. **Five** dispatches this round did exactly that and all five were right.

## Zone 2 — my assumptions; falsify them before building on them

a. ⭐ **The remedy calculus moved under this card, and I measured it — see my comment above.** Two gates landed this shift that owed **no** bare-root row at all, because both declared a subtree-glob population (`turbo.json/**`; `packages/**` + `examples/**`).
